answers.note: Strong, need-specific adaptations built on whole-class changes, with a timed four-step structure, a clear finish line and a realistic prep list for tomorrow.

Gives a ready-to-use scaffolded sheet that keeps the judgement, but per-need adaptations are only a brief table, the autistic student gets no model or example of a finished answer, and singling out is not addressed.
Thorough and practical: whole-class changes avoid singling anyone out, each need gets targeted adjustments, and a complete ready-to-print task with a 30-minute timed breakdown is provided.
Keeps every fact and all key terms with in-text definitions, short sentences, accurate conversions, plus headings, a glossary, questions and a note of what was kept.
Accurate and complete with a useful glossary and questions, but several sentences are long and multi-clause for a reading age of 9 and it drops the link between climate and biodiversity.
Clear, short-sentence rewrite keeping the facts, but the word 'biodiversity' is removed and there is no glossary, headings or teacher note.
Tight whole-class sheet with error codes, fixes, an annotated model and an in-lesson rewrite task, though the model wrongly claims 'himself' is repeated in Birling's quotation.
Excellent code-linked sheet with accurate quotations and context, an annotated model paragraph, code-specific 15-minute rewrite tasks and a stretch code for the capitalism students.
Well-structured sheet, codes and fully timed lesson with a rewrite task, but the analysis example claims a 'repeated focus on his own' that is not in the quoted line.
